title: "Clean" Code, Horrible Performance
summary: Benchmarks the canonical shapes example to show virtual dispatch and opaque objects make code many times slower than switch and table-driven versions; concludes clean code rules cost a decade of hardware gains.

assertions.quote: you immediately get what is effectively a 1.5 x performance increase for not really doing anything other than removing all of that extraneous stuff
there's no way you're doing any of that using clean code principles because just the nature of how you're going to organize your data
there is really no way to objectively assess whether these clean code ideas are good or bad
for a certain segment of the Computing industry the answer of why is software so slow it's because of quote unquote clean code
it's really easy to pull out common patterns when you look at them put together by function rather than by class
